settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Line 58 explicitly sets load-external-dtd=false, reducing external DTD-based XXE
Entity expansion depends on the underlying JAXP implementation defaults; many modern JDKs default to more restrictive behavior
getTextForElements/getTextForElement catch parse exceptions and return null, so failures do not crash the flow
safeGetParameter restricts which request parameters are read but not the parameter content
candidates.description: XmlUtils.getXmlReader() creates a SAXParserFactory/XMLReader and sets only namespaces, namespace-prefixes and 'load-external-dtd=false'. It does not set 'external-general-entities'/'external-parameter-entities' to false nor disable DOCTYPE declarations. The reader is used by getTextForElement/getTextForElements, which are called by SingleSignOutHandler.destroySession on the logout message value (back-channel: logoutRequest parameter; front-channel: base64+inflated SAMLRequest parameter) taken from the HTTP request via CommonUtils.safeGetParameter. Because these inputs are attacker-influenced (a POST body/GET parameter), a parser that still allows internal/external entity definitions can be abused for entity-expansion (billion-laughs style) or, where external entity resolution is reachable, SSRF/local file disclosure into the parsed text. Note the code explicitly disables external DTD loading, which mitigates the classic external-DTD variant but does not itself disable external general entities declared in an internal subset.
missing_evidence: Actual effective values of external-general-entities/secure-processing features at runtime (JDK version dependent)
No call-site proof that the parsed text is reflected anywhere besides SessionIndex matching
No test/configuration demonstrating the parser processes a malicious DOCTYPE internal subset
preconditions: Attacker can reach an endpoint where SingleSignOutFilter/SingleSignOutHandler is installed
Application processes attacker-supplied logoutRequest (POST) or SAMLRequest (GET) values
SAXParserFactory implementation honors/does not default-disable DOCTYPE/entity expansion features
candidates.title: XmlUtils SAX reader does not disable external general entities / DOCTYPE, used for SLO logout message parsing

counter_evidence: Only the first matching configured alias is returned; the attacker cannot inject arbitrary serverName text, only select among configured values
When 'service' is configured, constructServiceUrl returns it directly and this code is bypassed (line 272-273)
Line 219's 'host == "localhost"' is a latent bug but does not by itself grant attacker control
candidates.description: CommonUtils.findMatchingServerName splits the configured space-separated serverName list and returns the first entry whose lowercased value contains the request Host header (String.contains), then defaults to serverNames[0]. The Host header is attacker-controllable. A crafted Host that is a substring of a configured alias can cause selection of an unintended serverName, influencing the service URL used in redirects and ticket validation. Also, line 219 compares the Host header with '==' (reference equality) rather than equals(), which means the X-Forwarded-Host branch is effectively never taken for the intended localhost case, a logic inconsistency.
missing_evidence: Whether any deployment configures multiple serverName aliases
Whether the container/proxy normalizes or rejects arbitrary Host headers
Downstream impact of the selected service URL (ticket redirection target)
preconditions: serverName configured with multiple space-separated aliases
Attacker can control the Host header reaching the servlet container
candidates.title: Host header used with contains() to select serverName in constructServiceUrl

counter_evidence: Truncation reduces (not increases) the data handed to XmlUtils and yields no SessionIndex, so it does not cause a bypass
Content is then parsed as XML text only for the SessionIndex element
No demonstrated amplification: output is capped at 10x input
candidates.description: uncompressLogoutMessage base64-decodes the SAMLRequest value, allocates result = binaryMessage.length * DECOMPRESSION_FACTOR (10) and performs a single Inflater.inflate() call, then constructs the string from the returned length. If the payload inflates beyond decoded-length*10 the message is silently truncated, potentially dropping or corrupting the SessionIndex element. More importantly, this code path constructs buffers from attacker-controlled input without any size bound; a large base64 parameter produces a correspondingly large allocation before validation. Base64.decodeBase64 is invoked on the raw parameter with no length check, and the exception path wraps failures in a RuntimeException (line 271), which may surface as an error response.
missing_evidence: Whether an oversized allocation is practically reachable given container request-size limits
Whether the RuntimeException is handled and produces a safe response
Actual behavior of Inflater on malicious deflate streams (e.g., needDictionary/DataFormatException handling)
preconditions: SingleSignOutHandler front-channel logout path reachable via GET SAMLRequest parameter
candidates.title: SingleSignOutHandler.uncompressLogoutMessage uses fixed 10x buffer with single inflate() call

counter_evidence: Hostname verification still applies via the configured hostnameVerifier (defaults to the platform verifier, line 50)
The default SSL context still performs normal trust validation; only the custom keystore override is lost
Failures are logged at error level
candidates.description: createSSLSocketFactory() reads keyStoreType/keyStorePath/keyStorePass/certificatePassword and builds an SSLSocketFactory, but wraps the entire block in a catch that only logs (LOGGER.error) and then returns null. In configureHttpsConnectionIfNeeded, a null socket factory means setSSLSocketFactory is skipped (line 95-97), so the connection silently falls back to the JVM default SSL context. Also, if only some keystore properties are set, the code can NPE (e.g., certificatePassword may be null when keyStorePass is present, line 133-134) and degrade to the default context. The result is a silent downgrade of the intended client-certificate/trust configuration rather than a hard failure.
missing_evidence: Whether deployments rely on this factory for mutual TLS to the CAS server
Runtime behavior when only partial keystore properties are present
Whether a null return is treated as an error elsewhere by callers
preconditions: Misconfiguration or keystore load error occurs
hostnameVerifier may separately allow the trust to be weaker depending on configuration
candidates.title: HttpsURLConnectionFactory silently returns null SSLSocketFactory on keystore configuration failure

counter_evidence: The regex is the configured key, not attacker input, so ReDoS requires complex configured patterns
A default filter or normal chain runs when no match (lines 104-108), so absence of match is safe
candidates.description: DelegatingFilter.doFilter takes a request parameter value and, when exactMatch is false, evaluates parameter.matches(key) for each configured delegator key. If the configured keys are derived from/provide untrusted patterns, or if matching is intended to be exact, a non-exact configuration causes attacker-controlled input to be treated as a regex subject (and keys as regex). The value is used for decisions about which downstream filter runs. Note the pattern matching uses the configured key as the regex and the parameter as the input, so the attacker controls the input, not the pattern; risk centers on regex complexity against attacker input or on routing decisions.
missing_evidence: Whether any configured key is a catastrophic-backtracking pattern
Whether routing to a specific filter via crafted parameter has security impact
preconditions: Attacker can supply the requestParameterName value
candidates.title: DelegatingFilter compiles attacker-controlled parameter as a regular expression

counter_evidence: Sources are server-side init parameters, not request parameters
ReflectUtils.newInstance failures are caught for ignoreUrlPatternType
candidates.description: AuthenticationFilter.initInternal reads ignoreUrlPatternType from filter/context/JNDI init params. If it is not one of CONTAINS/REGEX/EXACT it is passed to ReflectUtils.newInstance as a fully-qualified class name (line 106). Likewise gatewayStorageClass and authenticationRedirectStrategyClass are instantiated reflectively (lines 119, 126). These values come from configuration (web.xml/context/JNDI), not directly from HTTP requests, so this is a configuration-injection/deserialization-adjacent surface rather than a remote-input vulnerability, but a party able to influence filter init parameters could instantiate arbitrary classes (subject to casting) with default constructors.
missing_evidence: Whether any deployment path allows request-controlled values to reach these init params
Class-loading side effects of candidate classes
preconditions: Attacker can influence web.xml/context-param/JNDI values read by the filter
A suitable class with a no-arg constructor is on the classpath
candidates.title: AuthenticationFilter ignoreUrlPatternType can instantiate arbitrary classes via reflection
